question.text: A <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> long wire is broken into two unequal parts <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math>. The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> part of the wire is stretched into another wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>W</mi></math>. Length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>W</mi></math> is twice the length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> and the resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>W</mi></math> is twice that of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math>. Find the ratio of length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>X</mi></math> and<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi></math>.

solution.text:
​​​​​​​

Resistance of a wire is given by R=ρLA, where, ρ is conductivity, L is length of wire and A is cross-sectional area of wire.

For a single wire, A and ρ are constant.

Thus, for parts X and Y, resistance, RXRY=lXlY.

When wire is stretched to double of its length, then resistance becomes four times, thus, RW=4RX=2RY.

Hence, the ratio is RXRY=12.

So,  lXlY=12
